entities.summary: Laodice II, was the wife of Seleucus II Callinicus. According to the express statement of Polybius, she was the sister of Andromachus and therefore the aunt of her husband. Laodice II bore Seleucus II Seleucus III Ceraunus and Antiochus III the Great. Polyaenus Strat. 8.61 has a curious story that may not be true, but calling Laodice another name: Mysta, he says "When Seleucus, surnamed Callinicus, was defeated by the Gauls at Ancyra in 237, and fell into the hands of the enemy, his wife Mysta threw aside her royal robe, put on the ragged dress of a lowly servant, and as such was sold amongst the prisoners.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Laodice II was a significant figure in the Seleucid Empire, playing a role in the succession of her husband's sons and contributing to the regional dynamics of the ancient Near East. Her story highlights the complexities of royal politics and the impact of personal relationships on imperial succession.
